Title: Utilizing machine learning to analyze trunk movement patterns in women with postpartum low back pain
Model / Method: CNN, Random Forest, MLP, LSTM, Stacked LSTM, SVR, Bagging, Optuna-optimized models
Main Finding: CNN and RF achieved perfect classification performance in the reported experiment
Limitation: Small and specific population; generalizability concerns
Research Gap: Need larger and more diverse clinical datasets

Title: Objective Pain Assessment Using Deep Learning Through EEG-Based Brain–Computer Interfaces
Pain Task: Pain detection and pain severity classification
Main Finding: Deep learning achieved strong performance for objective pain assessment from EEG
Research Gap: Need to investigate other modalities and generalization

Title: Empirical comparison of deep learning models for fNIRS pain decoding
Model / Method: CNN, LSTM, CNN-LSTM and classical ML
Main Finding: CNN-LSTM achieved the best reported performance
Limitation: Generalization to independent populations remains a concern
Research Gap: Further validation on independent populations and real-world settings

Title: Automated facial recognition system using deep learning for pain assessment in adults with cerebral palsy
Dataset: Multiple facial pain databases and CP-PAIN
Validation Strategy: Five validation splits including previously unseen users and CP-PAIN
Main Finding: InceptionV3 achieved the best reported CP-PAIN accuracy
Limitation: Small and challenging clinical dataset; subtle pain expressions
Research Gap: Need larger, diverse datasets and improved generalization

Title: Assessing the Impact of Prolonged Sitting and Poor Posture on Lower Back Pain: A Photogrammetric and Machine Learning Approach
Model / Method: DT, NB, LR, GLM, FLM, RF, GBT, DLNN
Main Finding: Machine learning can classify lower-back-pain-related conditions from posture features
Limitation: Snapshot measurements cannot establish pain development longitudinally

Title: Deep Learning-Based Instance Appraisable Model (EDi Pain) for Pain Estimation via Facial Videos: A Retrospective Analysis and a Prospective Emergency Department Study
Other Metrics: UNBC MAE 1.85, PCC 0.63; NTU MAE 1.48, PCC 0.22
Validation Strategy: Retrospective public dataset plus prospective clinical study
Main Finding: Demonstrated facial-video pain estimation in retrospective and prospective settings
Limitation: Weak labels and relatively low prospective PCC

Title: Acute Pain Recognition from Facial Expression Videos using Vision Transformers
Model / Method: ViViT with ResNet50 and ResNet50+3DCNN baselines
Main Finding: Vision Transformer approach demonstrated facial pain recognition on two datasets
Limitation: Performance remains moderate, especially on AI4PAIN
Research Gap: Further work needed for robust generalization

Title: Multimodal pain assessment with transformers
Dataset: Multimodal facial video and physiological signals
Limitation: Exact performance values require further extraction from the paper
Research Gap: Further investigation of efficient and generalizable pain assessment
